# NEXUS: test plan

[한국어](nexus.ko.md)

Stage 12 of CORTHEX’s own project. Status: execution in progress; all717 cases have scoped verdicts (692 pass,7 partial,18 not applicable,0 fail). Partial clauses remain unproved; adjudication is not full acceptance. Actual runs and original performance failures are retained below. English is the source and the Notion case database follows it. Inputs are stages 02–09, especially each active SPEC acceptance criterion, named OpenAPI response, hub command outcome and screen state. Phase-② editing/workshop flows FL-115/FL-116 are deferred with SPEC-134/SPEC-142.

From the design revision of 2026-11-11, this file also plans the 387 cases of the revision, TC-1408 to TC-1794, in [The design revision of 2026-11-11](#the-design-revision-of-2026-11-11): each is run by the task that builds its row, which writes the result in the case's row, and they are not in the counts above.

## How to read this file

`ID` is permanent, starting at TC-601; BUG starts at BUG-501. `From` is the acceptance criterion, API response, SCR state or REQ under test. `Task` writes/runs the case in its finishing PR. `Runs as` names the actual method. `Steps` describes the fixture/action, `Expected` includes the response and effects and `Last result` names environment, commit and evidence when run. not run means not run. A response example checked only with Prism is counted separately from development evidence.

From the design revision of 2026-11-11, a case may be written before its task: its `Task` then names the task that will build the row and run the case, or says `none yet (phase ②)` for a row that phase ②'s own plan gives a task.

For0.2.1, not applicable means that an exact legacy shared example cannot occur under that operation's declared input or role. It is excluded from passing evidence; its original row and verdict remain in the versioned applicability proof. Seven corrected endpoint-specific examples have new IDs TC-1311–1317.

## Where the cases run

- Server: Node built-in tests with in-memory SQLite/D1, Wrangler local D1, then corthex-nexus-dev behind Access. Contract tools live outside the repository: openapi-spec-validator 0.7.1, Prism 5.16.0, Schemathesis 3.39.16 with experimental OpenAPI 3.1.
- Hub: standard-library unittest, isolated home/project and fake local HTTP; Python 3.8 and latest on Linux/macOS/Windows, including real Git object fixtures.
- Views: Prism first, then the real development Worker; browser agents use Aside CLI where available, otherwise a named host browser tester. Start three isolated browser sessions and measure safe concurrency before increasing. No production writes.
- Every state: 320/1440 pixels, light/dark and English/Korean; page-check.js measurements and separately inspected screenshots.
- Credentials remain in this host’s secret store/environment. Access evidence records presence/empty only. Synthetic data is seeded per role and tester; this repository is never pushed without REQ-107 consent.
- From the design revision of 2026-11-11, a browser walk also leaves the user's own acts, and any write, off a project that is not synthetic (SPEC-200), and one case alone runs on the maintainer's server, on the maintainer's word (TC-1789).
- From the design revision of 2026-11-11, the revision's states are looked at at 390 and 1,440 pixels, and the workspace at 1,152 and 1,280 pixels too with each fold, as stage 08 draws them; the earlier cases keep their widths.

## Kinds of cases

| Kind | Coverage or reason |
| --- | --- |
| Access | Both real identities, wrong audience/kind, missing/expired sign-in, cross-site writes; refusal changes nothing. |
| Input | Required/blank/long/invalid/unknown fields, malformed UTF-8/JSON and direct API requests, plus CLI validation. |
| Target | Unknown/malformed/deleted project, part, picture, item and entry; never an accidental 500. |
| State changes | Reopen/settle/decide, proposal transitions, reflection reports, checkpoint withdrawal and recorded-state warnings. |
| Repeats | Lost replies, double writes, same ID and another request, repeated reports and seven-day expiry. |
| Concurrency | Interleaved pushes, two sessions/claims, simultaneous quota use, two hubs on one outbox and two part records. |
| Limits | Snapshot/body/text sizes, 30 projects, space text, open entries, bounded list totals and free CPU/query budgets. |
| Outside services | Network/timeouts/token refusal; editors, fonts and assets stay on the same Access-protected origin, served by the approved standalone runtime (or the separately tested Worker compatibility runtime); no external runtime service. |
| Data exposure | No identities except roles; no home paths/secrets; full proposal source only on own read; XSS remains text. |
| Empty and streamed answers | Empty hub, no picture/entries/to-do/outbox, HEAD no body; no streaming API is specified. |
| Screen states | Each declared state above at both widths/themes/languages; hash panels, drafts and editor fallback. |
| AI answers | Not applicable: NEXUS calls no AI model (REQ-121); no paid call is made. |

From the design revision of 2026-11-11, the kinds for the revision's rows are in [Kinds of cases of the revision](#kinds-of-cases-of-the-revision), with the reason where a kind has no case.

Current REQ-124/TASK-223 disposition: pass under the approved 2026-11-04 standalone definition, as recorded in TC-1270. The earlier free-Worker CPU trial failed at 83 ms against its 10 ms budget; its query/row evidence and contemporaneous pending decision remain historical entries below.

Nearest-rank P95 (rank19 of20) was DDD1399.2 ms, ERD1327.2 ms and sitemap1357.3 ms, each below3000 ms. ## Walking the flows

TASK-251 builds one run row per FL-101–FL-114 main/failure path and actual role, using the phase-① rows of each flow. Each tester gets isolated seed data and its own tabs; it records visible text/screenshots after each action and verifies expected data effects through the API/read-only query. Reports name commit, tool/version, widths, role/path, TC, works/fails/blocked, evidence and impressions separately. Working paths become e2e CI tests. FL-115 and FL-116 are not run: deferred phase ②.

From the design revision of 2026-11-11, the walk of the redesign's and the revision's screens is in [The walk in a real browser and the release decision](#the-walk-in-a-real-browser-and-the-release-decision): FL-113, FL-114, FL-117 to FL-119 and FL-127 are walked in a real browser on a synthetic project, and the testers' impressions are reported apart from the bugs. FL-115 and FL-116 stay not run until phase ② builds them.

## The release decision

The maintainer's 2026-11-04 conditional approval supersedes the original final release question: all specified gates must pass before main merges, production transition and tags. Finish the feasible active tasks and final-tree checks, retain incomplete flow/response/platform scopes and report remaining issues. If any release condition remains unmet, ask once with its numbers and wait before release. First repository upload still requires REQ-107 confirmation; local tests do not provide it.

From the design revision of 2026-11-11, what a later release needs from QA is D19 of stage 02, which the maintainer decided on 2026-11-12 as recommended: [The walk in a real browser and the release decision](#the-walk-in-a-real-browser-and-the-release-decision) writes it into cases, and no release is made under it without the maintainer's own go.

## Bugs

BUG-501 (TC-1269, SPEC-113/116): the temporary development module returned internal/500 while its default fetch was called with the verifier as receiver. A global-call wrapper fixed it; a host-receiver regression test and the real user/agent role trials pass. Fixed in this Access foundation bundle. This is a temporary-entrypoint failure, not evidence about unimplemented API operations. Preserve each failure with its TC/SPEC/SCR/API response, steps, expected/actual data effect, environment/commit, safe traceId and screenshot/API evidence. Impressions are recorded separately until the maintainer chooses to make them bugs/tasks.

From the design revision of 2026-11-11, the bugs that the review named as open, BUG-562 and BUG-595, each have a case that looks at them again before the release (TC-1794, TC-1793), and a bug that stays open at a release does so on the maintainer's word, by name (D19).

## Notes for later stages

Each implementation PR updates only the cases it actually ran and cites raw evidence. A server contract pass means provided; accepted additionally requires the real-server screen/flow. Default/internal mock cases, manual Access trials, CI matrix and image review remain distinct. Keep the source first, then update/read back Notion.

From the design revision of 2026-11-11: the builder runs each case of the revision with the task that its row names and writes the result into that row; a case whose row a decision drops is marked removed, with its ID kept; and phase ②'s own stage 12 adds the cases of its requests, API-161 to API-176, once they are planned forms in the contract (TASK-320).

## Access evidence (TASK-201)

Development Access on 2026-11-03 supplied ctx.access and the configured audience for both a real browser user and a service token. getIdentity could not distinguish them. The presence-only table and the verifier choice were written to stage 06 before authentication implementation. A pinned-team RS256/JWKS signature, issuer, audience and expiry check then verified both real assertion headers; no token, cookie, email or service client ID is retained.

The implementation was exercised through a temporary development entrypoint using the actual Access/Problem modules: user `/` 200, `/user-only` 200, `/agent-only` 403 agent_only; agent `/` 200, `/agent-only` 200, `/user-only` 403 user_only. Wrong audiences, forged/expired tokens, key rotation/outage, malformed assertions and missing/null sub use synthetic signed fixtures on Node 24.18.0, not altered real identities. Node tests are 29/29 on this branch (14 Access/Problem and 15 existing). A read-only code/security review found two issues in an earlier module version (unexpired-key cache lost on refresh failure and nonempty service name with missing/null sub); both were corrected and independently rechecked.

These are authentication foundation and temporary-entrypoint checks. app.js still uses its phase-1 routing: TASK-209 and TASK-210 remain in progress, and no API-101–API-132 response, page or flow is marked provided/accepted by this evidence.

Commit `51cc0d3` is the Access foundation tested above. The full Windows/Python 3.13 repository suite also passed 817 tests (14 skipped), and all four strict Claude plugin validations passed. The edited OpenAPI passes openapi-spec-validator 0.7.1. Full development API contracts and screens remain untested.

An additional 512 status checks over 256 SQLite-valid quoted names passed locally. |

| BUG-528 | SPEC-104, API-133 | Unsupported files and translations spent the 400-file picture budget. Supported originals are selected first; omitted supported files produce an explicit picture-partial check with their count and first path. |
| BUG-529 | SPEC-106 | Struck domain terms and events were resurrected. Removing struck text now also handles first/last/all-deleted timeline places without leaving arrows in surviving names or phantom events. |
| BUG-530 | SPEC-109, API-134 | Concurrent status commands could lose another writer's stage. The complete read-modify-replace operation now shares a native per-file guard across profiles and aliases; retry reloads current data and process exit releases the guard. A first stat-based Windows key split across Python 3.8/current device widths; both now use the same native directory identity API. |
| BUG-531 | SPEC-109, API-134 | A preplanted private guard-directory junction could leave guard metadata inside the repository. | BUG-533 | SPEC-107, TC-613 | One ALTER TABLE adding multiple foreign keys retained only the first and could borrow the second key's ON DELETE. Top-level comma actions are now parsed separately; composite-column, quoted-comma, default/restrict/set-null and later-cascade controls retain both targets, rules and source lines. |
| BUG-534 | REQ-149, TC-1271 | Two isolated mobile openings received 403 on the core module while the page/editor/font requests succeeded. The final prototype therefore completed only 18/20 Excalidraw openings. Root cause is under read-only account/response investigation; no Access policy is relaxed and no successful P95 is inferred from the remaining openings. |

## Transport, measurement and release decision of 2026-11-04

The maintainer approved edge caching of public content-hashed code, styles and fonts at the same configured origin (REQ-147). HTML, API, project data and refusals remain no-store. Code has no Set-Cookie or Vary:*, with unchanged CSP and whole-host Access. Even a cached object must not reach unauthenticated GET/HEAD callers. An edge HIT does not visit the origin, so origin verification is not claimed on every HIT.

Loading preserves the frame and surrounding layout. Distinguish first-preview and native-editor-ready states and timings.

TC-1318 and TC-1319 hold the planned operations and the counts that TASK-265 left: eight planned, 70 defaults and 32 operations. Each later task that marks its operations active writes its own counts in its cases, as TC-1328 does for TASK-266, TC-1334 for TASK-267, TC-1342 for TASK-268, TC-1350 for TASK-269, TC-1358 for TASK-270 and TC-1383 for TASK-271, which left none planned, 94 defaults and 41 operations, and those results stay as they were.

TC-1359 to TC-1373 are TASK-272's cases; a rule in their From is one of [stage 08's rules for the redesign's screens](../08-screens/nexus/README.md#the-redesigns-screens). Their browser cases ran the redesign's pages on the synthetic server of `nexus/test/view-server.mjs`, through an address of its own, and they cover what TASK-272 draws: the top bar, the bar of rule 15, the list of stages and the tabs. The first page's lists and the stage's own parts come with TASK-273 to TASK-277. Since TASK-271 the same suite opens the pages at their own addresses, where the server's handler serves them, and their results above stay as they were.

TC-1374 to TC-1384 are TASK-271's cases. They test where each address leads and what each page holds, not what the pages show, which TASK-273 to TASK-277 build; the redirects of 0.2's picture view and stage overview to the stage's page, SPEC-154's, come with TASK-278 ([stage 10](../10-wbs/nexus.md#moved-on-2026-11-08)). Running the browser suites for TASK-271 failed twice before the run of TC-1384: TC-1384's first check compared the overview's link as written, while its code writes links whole, so the check now compares the place that a link leads to; and TC-1373's click on the part switch missed once, since the fonts joined between reading the switch's place and the click, and the text above the switch, set again in them, moved it up, so that case now probes and clicks only after the fonts, as TC-1368 waits for them. In the run of TC-1384, with the fonts in, it found 5 controls in the stage's top bar and tabs, 11 in the list of stages, 2 in the part switch and 3 on the first page, as TC-1373 did; the switch stood 276 pixels from the top, where the run before, which passed before the fonts joined, had found it at 301 and 10 controls in the list.

TC-1385 to TC-1396 are TASK-273's cases. Their browser cases ran the first page on the synthetic server of `nexus/test/view-server.mjs` with `NEXUS_QA_HOME=1`, whose spaces without entries and without projects a cookie chooses. The suite answered the answers of #stale, #error and #permission, a failed reading and the failures of TC-1393 itself, and the fixture server answered the rest; each result says which. The page suite of TC-1367 now lets the first page's answers and order lose their wait, as TASK-273's code makes them work, and keeps the times in UTC; TC-1367's result above stays as it was, and TC-1396 is its run with TASK-273. The first page's search and its links to a stage's list and items wait for TASK-274 and TASK-277 ([stage 10](../10-wbs/nexus.md#left-on-2026-11-08)). Looking at the screenshots found the flag of a picture that is not current drawn wrong: its icon took the whole flag, since the small view's rule for its drawing took every SVG in it, and at 390 pixels its English word wrapped onto a second line over the count. The rule now takes only the drawing, and the flag keeps to one line, closer to the edge with a smaller icon in a phone's small view and its icon alone in one of 90 pixels or less; TC-1391's check of the flag found both faults before the fix.

TC-1397 to TC-1407 are TASK-274's cases. Their browser cases ran the workspace on the synthetic server of `nexus/test/view-server.mjs` with `NEXUS_QA_STAGE=1`, whose project `qa-stage` holds stage 02 with 450 synthetic requirements, three of them with talk, one in my turn, three left and a checkpoint passed in NEXUS that waits for its record; stage 05 with an open proposal and a pending reflection; stage 04 without items; and stage 03, which the project does not read; its project `qa-stage-unrecorded` has no recorded progress. The suite answered the failed readings, the refusals, the expired sign-ins, `write_id_reused` and `checkpoint_recorded`, and failed the next 200 once in each setting; the fixture server answered the rest, the passes, the withdrawals and the push again included; each result says which. The unit check of TC-1366 now lets a stage's controls wait for `list` and `record` and its rows lead to `#item=` and `#view=list&item=`, and the page suite of TC-1367 lets the list and the record lose their wait; their results above stay as they were, and TC-1407 is their run with TASK-274. A pictured stage shows its list until TASK-275 draws its picture, and the talk, the item and the search wait for TASK-276 and TASK-277 ([stage 10](../10-wbs/nexus.md#left-on-2026-11-09)). Looking at the screenshots found three faults, fixed before these runs: at 1,440 pixels the head's counts ended in an ellipsis, so the head now takes two lines, as stage 09 draws it, and the counts wrap, each whole; the grouping wrapped alone onto a line of its own, so the search and the grouping now keep together; and at 390 pixels Stage record stood at the left on a stage that the project does not read, so it now keeps to the right end of its line. Writing the browser cases found two more: the talk folded from 1,024 to 1,279 pixels could not be closed, since its Close comes with TASK-276, so Escape now folds it; and past 2,000 characters the checkpoint's words box said nothing, so it now says the limit. Running the browser suites found a fault that TASK-274 did not make: the first page's suite of TC-1389 was blocked in 3 of 8 runs on this branch and in 2 of 8 on `6576ade`, the commit before TASK-274, each time in the case of TC-1390, when the page went on to the next address while the suite still held its request for the fonts' stylesheet, so that Chrome answered the suite's Continue with "Invalid InterceptionId". That suite and TASK-274's now record such a request as dropped by the page, and 6 runs in a row then worked.

The runs of TASK-276 to TASK-311, with each task's suites, settings, faults found and deliberate breaks, are in [the run record of the revision's build](runs/2026-11-13-revision-build.md). Those up to TASK-302 moved there on 2026-11-13 so that this file, stage 12's source, stays within the 1 MiB that the pinned hub reads of a source file; each case's row here keeps its result.

With TASK-278 (2026-11-13), 0.2's picture view and stage overview answer `302` to the stage's page (SPEC-154), so no address serves their pages, and the five browser suites that opened them, of the picture view, its discussion, its errors, its code and the late screen, are retired; the cases that they ran keep their results as runs of 0.2, and TASK-319 matches what the redesign's tasks cover of 0.2's remaining acceptance. TC-1380, TC-1381 and TC-1384 now expect the redirects, and the page suite of TC-1367 opens 0.2's addresses as TC-1767 asks, in English and in Korean, on the fixture's project `qa-views`, which the fixture pushes again for the page suite with the two items that the addresses name: a cookie of the fixture sets the page's language, since a `302` keeps no query. The hub suite of TC-1766 now finds two projects on the server, not four, since the fixture no longer pushes the projects of two of 0.2's suites; its result above stays as it was.

## The design revision of 2026-11-11

An independent review of the whole NEXUS design found 41 points on 2026-11-11, and the maintainer asked the same day to fix the design from them ([the review's map](../reviews/2026-11-11-design-review.md)). Stages 01 to 10 are revised, and this section plans the cases that judge the revision's rows: 387 cases, TC-1408 to TC-1794, written before any task of the revision starts, from the flows, the acceptance criteria, the contract's planned forms and the screens' states, and not from code. None is run: nothing of the revision is built, and no task started before the revision's checkpoint, which passed on 2026-11-12 in the maintainer's own words. The cases above this section keep their rows and results as they are.

No case measures stage 02's [success measures](../02-prd/nexus.md#success-measures). The revision had planned a two-week trial for them, and on 2026-11-12 the maintainer decided not to run it (D20): the measures stay as what NEXUS is for, the rows of the loop are judged by their own cases here, and one case shows the loop once in the maintainer's own sessions (TC-1789). The decisions D16 to D19 were decided on 2026-11-12 as recommended, D16 to D18 at the revision's checkpoint. A case whose row followed one of them while it was open is run as written, and none is marked removed.

Of the 387 cases, 274 waited for no decision; 90 follow one of the decisions that were open until 2026-11-12, 13 D16, 74 D17 and 3 D18; 5, among the screens' states, hold one part under D17 beside the rest; and 18 are phase ②'s, with no task yet. The numbers were counted before the decisions by the script that built this section from the stage sources, which fails when a criterion, a planned example or a state row has no case; since D16 to D18 were decided as recommended, the 90 and the 5 are run as written.

### How the revision's cases are read

- The columns are those of [How to read this file](#how-to-read-this-file). `Task` is the task of [stage 10](../10-wbs/nexus.md#the-design-revision-of-2026-11-11) that builds the case's row and runs the case in its finishing pull request, where it writes the result with the commit, the environment and the evidence. `none yet (phase ②)` stands for a row that phase ②'s own plan gives a task. `Runs as` uses the words of the earlier cases.
- The kinds of evidence stay apart, as before: a synthetic handler, the standalone server with SQLite, D1 as Wrangler runs it locally, the development server behind Access, a read of the maintainer's server, the page-check's measurements and the screenshots that someone looked at. A mock's pass is never counted as a real server's.
- A case is a Must case when a requirement that its row serves is Must in stage 02. Phase ②'s rows are all Could, so there the cases of a part's core rows are that part's Must cases, once the checkpoint of phase ②'s stages 07 to 09 fixes [the core](../02-prd/nexus.md#the-core-of-the-editing-phase) (the review, finding 10).
- No case writes to the maintainer's server but TC-1789, the case of the maintainer's own task, which runs on the maintainer's word. A browser walk leaves the user's own acts, and any write, off a project that is not synthetic (SPEC-200).
- The result of a hub case names the test and the hub's commit that `hub-ref.json` pins, since the hub's tests live in `kodonghui/corthex` (the review, finding 35).

One case for each clause of the acceptance criteria of SPEC-187 to SPEC-210, and one for the clause that the revision added to each of SPEC-111, SPEC-115, SPEC-139 and SPEC-143. `Steps` is the clause itself, as [stage 04](../04-functional-spec/nexus.md) words it. The cases of SPEC-204 to SPEC-208 are phase ②'s: phase ②'s own plan gives them their tasks and puts SPEC-205 and SPEC-206, the drawing read back as a list of changes, first, since the maintainer decided D20 without a prototype.

### Server responses of the revision

One case for each named example of the contract's planned forms, 159 in all: the nine path items under `components.pathItems` and the two new operations, API-177 and API-178 ([stage 06](../06-api/nexus.md#how-the-contract-holds-the-planned-forms)). A case sends the example's request in its role to an isolated synthetic project and compares the answer with the contract, and a refusal changes no data. The cases of API-128 and API-159 follow D17. Until a task builds a form, TASK-279's check holds its examples to their schemas, which is a check of the contract and no result of these cases.

### The walk in a real browser and the release decision

D19 of [stage 02](../02-prd/nexus.md#open-decisions) says what a release needs from QA, from the next release on. The maintainer decided it on 2026-11-12, by choosing the recommendation on the decision card that asked it in the project's thread, and these cases write it down: every case of the release run and judged, with no failure of a Must case and no partial pass unless the maintainer passes that case by name; every screen that the release adds or changes walked in a real browser, with the testers' impressions shown to the maintainer apart from the bugs; and the go or no-go in the stage record, in the maintainer's own words, before the tag. The choices that were not taken are to keep the decision of 2026-11-04 for later releases, under which partial passes keep riding through, and to allow no partial pass and no exception, under which one condition that cannot be reproduced holds a release.

A walk is made by browser agents in a real browser, ego lite or Aside where the session has one and otherwise a named browser of the host, on a synthetic project that the walk's brief names (SPEC-200). What works and what does not are results and bugs. What was hard to use or looked wrong is an impression: it is listed apart, and the maintainer decides which impressions become bugs, tasks or changes to the requirements. The review found that the QA of 0.2 recorded no impressions and that the release went ahead of acceptance (findings 8 and 9).

### Checks on this plan

- Every clause of the acceptance criteria of SPEC-187 to SPEC-210 has one case, and so has each of the four clauses that the revision added to earlier rows: 96 cases.
- Every named example of the contract's planned forms has one case, 159, read from `docs/06-api/nexus.openapi.yaml`; and every state row of stage 08's revision has one, 28.
- Every case names a SPEC, a REQ or an FL in `From`, and a task of stage 10 that is not taken out, or `none yet (phase ②)`, in `Task`. The IDs run from TC-1408 to TC-1794 without a gap, after the last case above.
- Of the 18 flows that the revision changed or added, 16 are named in the `From` of a case. FL-107 and FL-110 are not: the revision added to each one sentence that names the flows of the redesign that take its steps over (FL-117, FL-119), whose cases judge them, and changed no step.
- The English and Korean copies have the same lines, IDs, code and links. Nothing was run against a server, a hub or a browser: these are cases, and no case has a result.

### For the revision's checkpoint

1. D19, which the maintainer decided on 2026-11-12 as recommended: a release needs every case run and judged, the walk in a real browser with its impressions, and the go or no-go in the stage record before the tag.
2. The plan's shape: 387 cases written before the tasks, each run by the task that builds its row, and none run yet.
3. What the plan leaves out: no case measures the success measures (D20), and phase ②'s requests, API-161 to API-176, get their response cases in phase ②'s own stage 12, once they are planned forms in the contract (TASK-320).

## The group 4 walk's findings (2026-11-13 KST)

Found while four browser agents walked the revision's group 4, TASK-295 to TASK-302, on the synthetic server: the first page's checkpoint request and its pass, the pass in the stage's record, a pass's refusals and the loop's two times. All five came with group 4's pages and are fixed; the suites `home` and `pass` and `nexus/test/api-pass-kind.test.js` keep them fixed. The agents' walk, with its rows, impressions and evidence, is in [its run report](runs/2026-11-13-group4-flows.md).

| ID | Title | Trace | Evidence and state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BUG-606 | The first page's pass shrank while it was sent, and a second press opened the request | SCR-110#normal, SPEC-196, FL-117 | While it is sent, the pass says "Sending…" and is announced as disabled, so that a second press sends nothing. From 1,024 pixels the entry's buttons sit at its end, and "Sending…" is shorter than "Pass the stage 05 checkpoint": the button shrank from 224 to 94 pixels, and "Open the request" slid 130 pixels to the right, under the pointer. The browser agent of the row G4/A3 pressed the pass twice at 1,440 pixels in light English: the second press opened the request's talk, so that the page left before it showed the pass, which the server held once. In Korean at 1,440 pixels, and at 390 where each button takes the line's width, the pointer stayed on the pass. A button now keeps at least its own width while it is sent, with "Sending…" over its own words, which keep their room unseen. Fixed in `8fbd75f`; the suite `home` keeps it (`answers-stay-in-place-until-the-page-loads-again`, TC-1705). |
| BUG-607 | The passed entry's Stage record opened the stage without its record | SCR-110#normal, SCR-112, SCR-113, FL-117 | After a pass the entry stays, marked "Checkpoint passed. You can withdraw it in the stage record until it is recorded.", with Stage record, a link to the stage's record. The link opened the stage's workspace with the record closed, the ERD and its talk at 1,440 pixels and the list at 390, so that the checkpoint and its Withdraw took another press of Stage record, and no address opened the record. The browser agent of the row G4/A3 found it at 1,440 pixels in light English and at 390 in dark Korean. The link is now `/p/{project}/{part}/{stage}#record`, which opens the record once the page's code runs; closing the record takes `#record` out of the address. Fixed in `8fbd75f`; the suite `home` keeps it (`answers-stay-in-place-until-the-page-loads-again`, TC-1705). |
| BUG-608 | A second press in the stage's record while it read again sent another pass | SCR-112#normal, SCR-113#normal, SPEC-194, FL-113 | The record's pass is off while it is sent, but between the server's answer and the record's reading again it could be pressed, still naming the request as the record had shown it. The browser agent of the row G4/C2 tapped the pass twice at 390 pixels in dark Korean on 04: the second tap went with a new write ID as the first was answered, the server refused it with `409` `request_changed`, and the record showed that refusal under the checkpoint that had just passed. On 05, whose request was settled already and whose button said Pass again, the same double tap recorded two checkpoints 37 milliseconds apart. After a pass or a withdrawal, the pass and Withdraw now stay off until the record has read again. Fixed in `8fbd75f`; the suite `pass` keeps it (`a-second-press-while-the-record-reads-again-390-ko`, TC-1713, TC-1716). |
| BUG-609 | A pass from Chromium without a head was recorded as another browser's | SCR-112#normal, SPEC-195, REQ-283 | Chromium without a head, as Playwright 1.63 launches it, names the brands HeadlessChrome and Chromium in its client hint `Sec-CH-UA`. The server took any brand but Chromium for another browser, so every pass of the walk was recorded as "another browser", while the same browser's User-Agent counts as Chrome, and TASK-299's test counts Chromium alone as Chrome. The browser agents of the rows G4/A3 and G4/C2 saw it in each of their settings. HeadlessChrome is now of Chrome's family, as in the User-Agent, and a brand of its own beside it is still another browser. Fixed in `8fbd75f`; `nexus/test/api-pass-kind.test.js` keeps it. |
| BUG-610 | A checkpoint request on a part that left the snapshot could be neither passed nor opened | SCR-110#error, SCR-111#error, SPEC-143, SPEC-196 | My turn gathers a space's open comments, those on a part that the project's snapshot no longer holds too. The request on such a part offered the pass and "Open the request": the pass was refused with `404` `part_not_found`, whose message offered "Open the request" too, and that address is SCR-111#error's message page, since the part's stage has no page. The request stayed in my turn, and NEXUS offered no way to open, answer or close it. The browser agents of the rows G4/A1 and G4/B4 found it at 1,440 pixels in light English and at 390 in dark Korean. Such an entry now links to no talk and offers no pass: it says "This part is not in the project's snapshot." and keeps its answers in place, with Mark answered for a comment, which closes it as answered (API-120); a refusal of it shows as the other answers' do, and `no_kind` without Try again, as in the talk. Opening such a part's talk instead would change what the stage pages answer, API-152 and API-158, for the maintainer to choose. Fixed in `8fbd75f`; the suite `home` keeps it (`answers-stay-in-place-until-the-page-loads-again`, `repeats-keep-their-write-id-390-ko-dark`, TC-1708). |

## The group 7 walk's findings (2026-11-14 KST)

Found while two browser agents walked the revision's group 7, TASK-310 to TASK-312, on the synthetic server: the project's data, its export and the removal of a project. All three came with group 7's panel and are fixed; the suite `data` keeps them fixed.

| ID | Title | Trace | Evidence and state |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| BUG-611 | Closed, the project's data opened from the phone's sheet of stages came back to the sheet and lost the rest of the address | SCR-130, SCR-111#normal, FL-118 | Under 1,024 pixels "Project data" is in the sheet of stages, which the stage's name in the top bar opens at the address `#stages`. The panel opened from there as a new step of the browser's history after `#stages`, so that Close and the back button, which take that step back, came back to `#stages`: the sheet showed again over the stage, and the sheet's own Close, `#stage`, left the rest of the address out while the stage still showed it. The browser agent of the row G7/A2 found it at 390 pixels in light English with an item open in the list: `#view=list&item={id}&data` closed to `#stages`, then `#stage`; at 1,440 pixels in dark Korean Close kept `#view=list&item={id}`. Chosen in the sheet, the panel now takes the sheet's place in the history, as a stage chosen there does: Close takes `data` out in place and the sheet stays closed, the back button comes back to the stage before the sheet with the rest of its address, and the focus returns to the stage's name in the top bar, which opens the sheet again. Fixed; the suite `data` keeps it (`normal@` in its four settings at 390 pixels, `addresses@390-dark-ko`, TC-1764). |
| BUG-612 | The removal's confirmation opened with its heading above the sheet's visible part | SCR-130#removal, FL-114 | On a phone "Remove this project" sits under the sheet's fold, so that the user scrolls the sheet to reach it, and the confirmation, drawn in the data's place, opened at that scroll: its heading "Remove {project} from this server", which takes the focus, and with a long name "This deletes:" too, were above the sheet's visible part, and the user saw a list of IDs first. The focus moved there without scrolling anything. The browser agent of the row G7/B6 found it at 390 pixels in light English and in dark Korean, the confirmation opening 81 to 170 pixels down. The panel's body now scrolls the focused control into its sight, the body alone and never the page behind it: the confirmation shows from its heading, and Cancel shows "Remove this project" again. Fixed; the suite `data` keeps it (`limits@390-dark-ko`, TC-1726). |
| BUG-613 | The removal's confirmation broke "{n} of {total}" across two lines, and a long name crowded the removal's button | SCR-130#removal, FL-114 | With 23 open comments the confirmation lists 20, with "{n} of {total}" after the list's name. At 1,440 pixels in dark Korean, where a single list keeps a column of half the panel, its Korean words "23개 중 20개" broke after "중". With the long-named project the removal's button wraps its words onto two lines inside 46 pixels, and they nearly touched its border. The browser agent of the row G7/B6 found both, at 1,440 pixels in dark Korean and at 390 in light English and dark Korean. "{n} of {total}" now stays on one line, and the confirmation's two buttons keep 8 pixels above and below their words where they kept 4; the suite measures at least 6 pixels between the words' lines and the button's edges. Fixed; the suite `data` keeps it (`limits@` at 1,440 pixels in light English and dark Korean and at 390 in dark Korean, TC-1726). |
